title.narrative: Social Support for Gender Empowerment and Resilience (SP GEAR) 'Amai Titukuke'

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the Action is to support the Government of Malawi in empowering Malawi¿s poorest and most vulnerable girls and women.

¿   Component 1: Strengthening of the social protection system as a whole with emphasis on supporting the implementation and on enhancing the effectiveness and efficiency of the Social Cash Transfer Programme (SCTP). 

¿     Component 2: Enhanced resilience and livelihoods of women from vulnerable households through cash+ economic empowerment activities.

Component 3: Enhanced access to social services by women and girls from vulnerable households.

title.narrative: National Gini index

description.narrative: The Gini index provides a summary measure of the degree of inequality and may be calculated using either income or consumption data. It measures the extent to which the distribution of income or consumption among individuals or households within an economy deviates from a perfectly equal distribution. The Gini index is the Gini coefficient expressed as a percentage ranging from 0 which represents perfect equality to 100 which implies perfect inequality. For methodology see: https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SI.POV.GINI.

title.narrative: Country score according to the Gender Inequality Index

description.narrative: This index measures gender inequalities in three important aspects of human developmentreproductive health, measured by maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rates; empowerment, measured by proportion of parliamentary seats occupied by females and proportion of adult females and males aged 25 years and older with at least some secondary education; and economic status, expressed as labour market participation and measured by labour force participation rate of female and male populations aged 15 years and older. The GII is built on the same framework as the IHDIto better expose differences in the distribution of achievements between women and men. It measures the human development costs of gender inequality. Thus the higher the GII value the more disparities between females and males and the more loss to human development.
